seen.extent: Handwritten station logs of 25 Jul - 4 Aug 1914 start at p. 56. Pages 56, 58, 60, 62, 66 and 70 carry several messages each of 10-letter code words, 5 to 40 words a message, e.g. p. 60 ASB (Scharnhorst) to KCA (Yap), 3 Aug: 'Asintjoung jopsimonado ...'. Total word count not measured. Wheatley's report (pp. 50-53) says copies of all messages of 25 Jul - 4 Aug are attached.
seen.cipher: Artificial 10-letter code words copied by Australian operators from German wireless, with plain German (some with English) in between. Wheatley, 19 Apr 1916, p. 53: 'These were all in the same code, which is evidently a code for the use of men-of-war and important land stations only. It differs very considerably from the Handels Verkehr Buch'. The code-word messages on pp. 56, 58, 60, 66 and 70 have no decipherment written with them. Two decodes are on the leaves: p. 62, one 7-word message glossed in German and English ('From Cruiser squadron. You are to go to Caroline Isles'), and p. 75, 4-letter groups (VGHA OHAG PDLW ...) glossed. So this lead covers the unglossed code-word messages only. Pages 170 and later seen are plain-language translations and minutes.

prior_art.lasry: GL.htm (targets/gramont1529) grep for Scharnhorst, HVB, Wheatley, Spee: no hits. The web search naming Lasry and 1914 German naval messages returned no Lasry work on it.
prior_art.edition: No edition of these logs found. Jose's Official History vol. IX and Corbett surfaced only as background and were not opened at these messages; neither is known to print the code-word texts. Admiralty telegrams of Aug 1914 on archivfuehrer-kolonialzeit concern ship movements, not these messages.
prior_art.literature: navyhistory.au on Wheatley quotes his 1934 paper: most intercepts were 'in an unknown code' and filed; he later decoded 10-letter HVB groups (two 5-letter parts) under a changed key, on Melbourne Cup Day 1914. That is HVB squadron traffic, and his 1916 report separates this men-of-war code from HVB. NOT opened: Phelps, Australian Code Breakers (2020), and Wheatley's account AWM252 A228, either of which might say more; Room 40 files not searched.

lead_updates.title: German wireless intercepts by Australian stations, 25 Jul - 4 Aug 1914, in the men-of-war 10-letter code (Scharnhorst, Yap, Tsingtau, Nauru, Berlin), with Wheatley's report of 19 Apr 1916
lead_updates.correspondents: SMS Scharnhorst, Admiral Berlin, stations Yap, Tsingtau and Nauru, SMS Planet, SMS Geier; copied at Thursday Island, Port Moresby, Cooktown, Roebourne and others
lead_updates.folio_note: 338 pages digitised; station logs from p. 56; Wheatley report pp. 50-53; about 21 pages viewed 3 Nov 2026. The Dutch minutes of the old lead are only pp. 3 and 8.
